messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point numbers have a finite precision, so when two operands are added the result is rounded to the nearest representable value. Because rounding can discard low‑order bits, the intermediate sum in \((a+b)+c\) may differ from the intermediate sum in \(a+(b+c)\), causing the final rounded results to diverge. Thus the rounding errors introduced at each step break the mathematical associativity of addition in floating‑point arithmetic.
